limited

/LIM-ih-tid/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Limited means restricted in size, amount, or extent; not extensive.

Limited means restricted in size, amount, or extent — like a tiny diner whose menu offers only five dishes, and not one more.

Example

Jae's phone plan comes with limited data, so he saves videos for home Wi-Fi to stay under the monthly cap.

The plan sets a fixed boundary on how much data Jae can use. Limited signals that a definite cap or border restricts the amount — cross it and you're cut off.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

restricted: Restricted means kept within set bounds by a rule or authority — restricted access, a restricted area. It points at who may pass or use something. Limited points at how much there is: a limited menu, limited seating. Access is restricted; amounts are limited, whoever is allowed near them.

narrow: Narrow means small in range or scope — a narrow choice of topics, a narrow definition, narrow interests. It measures breadth, not quantity. Limited measures an amount against a boundary someone set: limited funds, limited seats. A narrow menu offers few kinds of dish; a limited one caps how much exists.

capped: Capped means given a fixed upper limit that cannot be exceeded — capped data, capped enrollment, salaries capped by league rules. It stresses the ceiling itself. Limited is broader: it says the amount is held down, with or without a stated number. Everything capped is limited, but limited things need no exact cap.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

boundless: without any limit

extensive: covering a great range or amount

Where it sits · how far the amount is held down — finite → limited → minimal

finite vs. limited: A finite supply has an end point but can still be generous; a limited supply is noticeably held in check.

minimal vs. limited: Minimal goes further than limited — a minimal supply is the barest amount possible, scraping right against zero, while a limited one still leaves you something to work with.

The pieces

Root — limit

Suffix — -ed

Suffix — -ed: adjective-forming: having been given that quality

Put it together

Put it together: A limited thing has had a limes — a boundary line — drawn around it, and nothing inside may spill past the border.

Use the root in a new word: delimit

Use the root in a new word: delimit: The surveyors arrived at dawn to delimit the new property before construction began.

Word Choice

Neutral / everyday

Limited stresses that a boundary has been set on purpose: a limited menu, limited seating, a limited-time offer. It pairs naturally with "to" for whoever falls inside the line — entry is limited to members. Compared with plain small, limited implies someone or something drew the line.
